summary:
Turn 97 released the run's local work as its window closes, with everything recorded and the two decisive capacities exhausted.

Why the stop. The investigation is complete as far as its authorization allows. Audit units and semantic reviews are both exhausted: the end-to-end client-reply artifact (executed as 6baf5b7715294d88a8f4a36e085ebd04) cannot receive the review that would confirm it, and the reader-side observation obtained by exploration (5b9267ea51d742f9a6fdcfb7a6594990) cannot be fixed as a claim with its own artifact. The stop is scoped to the focus, so unfinished units, unresolved questions and the attribution issue remain visible rather than being closed by it.

What the run delivered. Twelve claim families with executed, mostly reviewed artifacts: nine confirmed violations or consequences — C1 (a recovery ignores a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED and commits a NOOP vector for it, reproduced on a driven proposal/commit history), C3 (that divergence reaching the applied state on the same history), C2 (the durable metadata record loses the bal value), C4 (a legal NOOP commit terminates a restarted owner through a nil dereference, on a constructed history), C6 (the promoted-leader variant of C1), C7 (the accept handler's rejection branch is unreachable, so a rejected round waits out the timeout), C9 (the recorder writes the recovering replica's own row's metadata, or dereferences nothing), C10 (a value beyond the 16-bit length field is truncated, displaces the following commands, panics the receiver's decoder, and — as the exploration observed — makes the production peer reader exit while a non-verbose configuration clears liveness silently), C11 (replica construction dereferences a failed probe dial, so an environment without a route to the probe cannot start a replica), C12 (the documented transitive-conflict skipping is inert) — plus two bounded no-violation protections: C5 (an owner that survives a NOOP recovery re-proposes the operation and, per the executed artifact, answers the client end to end) and C8 (the executor timeout enqueues a blocked instance and the enqueued entry starts a real recovery). The map is current at version 20, every file in the analysis roots has been read, and several early limitations were retired by later scenarios rather than left standing.

What remains, with its status. Two items need capacity rather than investigation: one semantic review for the pending client-reply artifact, and unit-plus-review capacity to fix the reader-side exit as a claim whose artifact observes it through a controlled expectation. Three items are deployment questions that decide whether findings are live (enabling the latency file, durable recording, or the transitive-skip flag). Two candidates stay paused with scoped resume conditions (accept-status semantics, client retry), and the attribution issue on the superseded C1 artifact has no mechanism the validator accepts, so it remains permanently visible bookkeeping whose substance already lives in the amended claim and in C3. Throughout, no requirement was weakened, no history was invented, and contrary evidence and inference boundaries were kept explicit rather than smoothed over.
